$comment: Scenarios where KovaaK's own aim type is wrong, and the measurement that says so. KovaaK's /scenario/popular is authoritative for Clicking / Tracking / Switching and is preferred over everything else by tools/generate_seed.py, because a benchmark author's category name is a sub-category as often as a category and guessing from a description was measurably wrong on 6 of Voltaic's 18. That preference is right. It is not infallible, and where it is wrong the error is not cosmetic: aim_type is the column find-match partitions the queue on, so a scenario mislabelled here is graded by the season as one skill and matched as another. It is also an input to deriveSubskills, which keys the sub-skill on (label, aim type), so one wrong aim type sends the scenario to the wrong sub-skill as well.
$statistic: Shots per kill, from the kill table of real runs. It measures exactly one thing: whether a target dies to a single shot or to sustained fire. That is a fact about the weapon, not about the aiming skill, and treating it as more than that is the mistake this file has to avoid.
$whatItCanSettle: One thing, in both directions. A scenario firing ~1 shot per kill cannot be Tracking, because tracking a target to death takes sustained fire - measured, the lowest genuinely-tracking scenario in the corpus is waldoTS at 32.1 and the median is 1,887. A scenario firing tens or hundreds of shots per kill cannot be Clicking, because clicking kills in one shot - measured, all 191 correctly-labelled clicking scenarios in the corpus sit between 1.0 and 1.3. Both are refutations, and a refutation is all this statistic gives.
$whatItCannotSettle: Which of the remaining two a scenario is. One shot per kill is equally consistent with Clicking and with one-shot target switching; heavy sustained fire is equally consistent with Tracking and with multi-shot target switching. The benchmark labels decide that second question. `namedBy` records every (benchmark, label) pair for the scenario verbatim, including the unhelpful ones - Viscose files Popcorn MV under Precision, which is a quality rather than a category - so a reader can see how strong the support actually is rather than take the word 'agreeing' for it.
$refusals: A correction needs its measurement to REFUTE the assigned label by a factor of ten, not merely sit near its edge. It needs at least one benchmark that names the scenario, and `namedBy` is checked pair by pair against the committed definitions so a claim of support cannot be invented - the check caught exactly that while this file was being written. A correction that agrees with KovaaK's is refused rather than ignored, because a correction nobody is checking is how a wrong label becomes permanent. npm run validate:aimtypes re-derives every figure below from the stats folder and fails if the separation has closed.
$subCategory: Deliberately not recorded here. The sub-skill is derived from (benchmark label, aim type) by tools/deriveSubskills.ts, so fixing the aim type fixes the sub-skill on its own - domiSwitch went from Linear Clicking to Evasive Switching with no sub-skill written anywhere. Naming it here as well would be a second source of truth for a field that already has one.

measurement.statistic: shots per kill, summed over every kill row in every local run whose filename begins '<scenario> - '. The exact prefix matters: matching '<scenario>*' instead sweeps in every variant sharing the stem, which is how the first draft of these figures had VT DotTS Intermediate S5 at 33.6 over 28,299 kills rather than 40.2 over 6,126. Splitting the filename on ' - ' instead is also wrong, and loses every scenario whose own name contains it - Star Tracking Regen - @wa11p1per among them.
measurement.source: the KovaaK's stats folder, parsed by src/core/stats/parseStatsFile.ts
measurement.corpus: 365 of the scenarios KovaaK's publishes have local runs: 197 labelled Clicking, 72 Target Switching, 60 Tracking.

reference.$comment: The bands the statistic separates, measured on scenarios whose aim type nobody disputes. Only the Clicking band is tight; Tracking and Switching overlap each other heavily, which is exactly why this file refuses to choose between them.

Clicking.range: 1.0 to 1.3 across all 191 correctly-labelled clicking scenarios

Switching.range: about 40 for the multi-shot ones; one-shot switching sits down at 1.5

domiSwitch.why: 177 shots per kill against the 1.0 to 1.3 every correctly-labelled clicking scenario in the corpus produces. The weapon is a Poke-Drill and the bot is a regen_dot: the target carries 55 health and regenerates 0.3s after damage stops, so a single click cannot eliminate anything. Four benchmarks that name it all file it under evasive switching, and the community thread cited in scenario_rationale.json names it as one of the two evasive-switching references.

domiSwitch Easy.why: The same scenario with larger or slower targets, measured over 1,900 kills, and the same Poke-Drill against a regenerating target. Corrected alongside its sibling because leaving it would put one half of a lineage in Clicking and the other in Switching, which is worse than either answer on its own: the weakness map and the sub-skill queues read this column, and a lineage split across two categories is invisible to both.

domiSwitch Easier.why: The third member of the domiSwitch lineage, same Poke-Drill against the same regenerating dot, 93.3 shots per kill over 198 kills. Viscose Benchmarks S2 files it under Post-Flick, which is a switching label. Corrected for the same reason as its siblings: a lineage split across two categories is invisible to both the weakness map and the sub-skill queues.

domiSwitch Avasive.why: 161 shots per kill with a lightning gun against the same regen_dot bot. Anima Micro v2 files it under Micro-Switching, which is a switching label. The sample is one run and 25 kills, which is thin - it is corrected anyway because the refutation does not depend on precision: at 161 shots per kill it would have to be wrong by a factor of a hundred to be a clicking scenario, and the weapon is not one a clicking scenario uses.

Star Tracking Regen - @wa11p1per.why: 225 shots per kill with a lightning gun at a regenerating target. Aimerz+ Evasive Switching files it under Evasive Switch. The same thin-sample caveat as domiSwitch Avasive applies and the same answer: a hundred-fold refutation does not need a large sample. Its sibling Star Tracking Regen 40% Larger carries the same Clicking label and has no local runs, so it is listed under pending rather than corrected.

Popcorn MV Easier.why: 1.4 shots per kill with a pistol. A tracking scenario cannot kill in one shot - the lowest genuinely-tracking scenario in the corpus is waldoTS at 32.1, twenty-three times higher, and the tracking median is 1,887. So the Tracking label is refuted by this scenario's own measurement. Which of the other two it is comes from the lineage rather than from this variant: snakbox files Popcorn MV Intermediate under Dynamic Clicking, and Popcorn is Voltaic's own dynamic clicking scenario, described in the Season 5 notes as tuned to focus on reaction rather than smoothness. This variant's own labels - Jade Palace's Arc and Viscose's Precision - describe the movement, not the category.

Popcorn MV Medium.why: The same lineage and the same one-shot pistol, 1.6 shots per kill over 788 kills, twenty times below the lowest tracking scenario measured, so Tracking is refuted here on its own evidence. Clicking rather than one-shot switching comes from the lineage, as for Easier: snakbox files the Intermediate variant under Dynamic Clicking. Viscose's own label here is Precision, which is a quality rather than a category.

Popcorn MV Intermediate.why: The same lineage and the same one-shot pistol, 1.9 shots per kill over 224 kills, seventeen times below the lowest tracking scenario measured. This is the variant carrying the lineage's direct support: snakbox files it under Dynamic Clicking, which is the category the other two inherit.

pending.$comment: Measured as inconsistent with the label KovaaK's assigns, and NOT corrected. Each needs a judgement this file's rule deliberately will not make on its own. Listed so they are visible rather than rediscovered.

1w4t_vbr_pokeball Raspberry.why: The best-sampled disagreement in the corpus - 5,902 kills - and the one that must not be acted on. Every other correction here overrules KovaaK's while its benchmarks agree with the correction. This one would overrule KovaaK's AND Aimerz+ Static Clicking, which files it under Static Clicking. The statistic only refutes 'kills in one shot'; it cannot tell a static-clicking scenario played with a drill weapon from a switching one, and both sources say the former. Needs somebody who has played it.

Star Tracking Regen 40% Larger.why: Sibling of a corrected scenario and almost certainly the same mislabel, but there are no local runs of it and this file does not correct on inference. It will be corrected the first time somebody runs it.

domiSwitch Hard.why: Its three siblings measure 93.3, 136.6 and 177.4 shots per kill on the same Poke-Drill against the same regen_dot bot, and the base scenario is corrected to Switching on that evidence - but no benchmark names this cut and nobody here has played it, so there is nothing to measure and this file does not correct on inference. It is no longer in the pool: it was the domiSwitch family's Expert rung until the board floor took it out, on 804 entries against the 1,667 an Expert window needs. Kept here because the mislabel is real whether or not this season grades it, and one run settles it.
